column3: NKJV has “Your Son also,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “that the Son may glorify You.”
NKJV has “I have finished,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the participle “having finished.”
Close to the Greek; “ask” is rendered “pray.”
NKJV has “keep through Your name those whom You have given Me,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “keep them in Your name, which You have given Me.”
NKJV includes “in the world” and has “Those whom You gave Me I have kept,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “in Your name, which You have given Me, and I guarded them.”
Close to the Greek; “the evil” is rendered “the evil one.”
NKJV has “Your truth,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the truth.”
NKJV has the future “will believe,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the present “are believing.”
NKJV includes “one” in “one in Us,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “in Us.”
NKJV has “they also whom You gave Me,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “that which You have given Me.”
